samples.question: The picture shows three coloured cords lying on white paper - one red, one green and one blue - together with several solid black pegs. Each cord is a single curve that is pinned to the paper at its own two ends; no cord touches another cord and no cord touches a peg. Now imagine pulling one cord tight, keeping its own two pinned ends exactly where they are: the cord sweeps across the paper and, with nothing in its way, ends up lying along the straight line that joins those same two pinned ends. A peg gets in the way of that pull exactly when the peg lies inside the area shut in between that cord as it is drawn and the straight line joining that same cord's own two pinned ends; that straight line is not drawn in the picture. Pegs outside that shut-in area never get in the way, and the other two cords never get in the way. Exactly one of the three cords can be pulled completely straight with no peg in the way; each of the other two shuts at least one peg inside. Which cord can be pulled completely straight - red, green or blue?
